# Yundera/AppStore — Lidarr

**Verdict: ERRORED · top severity Major · risk score 13** — the static half completed; the functional half could not run because **no demo instance was usable** (infra, not an app fault).

**Audit date:** 2026-08-03 · **Store version:** `lscr.io/linuxserver/lidarr:3.1.0` · **Compose:** `Apps/Lidarr/docker-compose.yml@main` (blob `77689b92`) · **Scope:** `n-a` (no compose_base — audit, not a PR) · **Depth requested:** full

---

## Summary

Lidarr's compose is a clean copy of the shipped Servarr family pattern (identical in structure to `Apps/Sonarr`, `Apps/Radarr`, `Apps/Prowlarr`): pinned image, correct Caddy/`pcs` wiring, complete store metadata, and all app state mapped under AppData. Three checklist deviations were found (1 Major, 3 Minor), none of them security- or data-loss-class, so **no Critical finding exists**.

The audit is nevertheless returned as **errored**, not as a compliance verdict: `depth=full` requires every mandatory functional phase to run, and **zero phases could be executed** — both demo PCS instances were down. Per the Functional Review Protocol's binding 2026-07-17 amendment (rule 4) and the orchestrator's binding 2026-07-07 amendment (rule B4), a mandatory phase that is `errored` can never yield `compliant`, and infra failure must not be recorded as a verdict about the app. This is a **retry**, not a judgement on Lidarr.

---

## Tech & Documentation (static review — completed)

### Passing checklist items

| Item | Verdict | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Specific version tag (no `:latest`) | **pass** | `lscr.io/linuxserver/lidarr:3.1.0`; tag independently verified to exist in GHCR (manifest HTTP 200) |
| No hardcoded credentials | **pass** | Only `TZ: $TZ`; no inline passwords, tokens or secrets |
| Data mapped to appropriate `/DATA` subdirs | **pass** | `/DATA/AppData/lidarr/config`, `/DATA/Media/Music`, `/DATA/Downloads` — nothing outside `/DATA` |
| **Static persistence check** (all actual state locations mapped) | **pass** | LinuxServer Lidarr keeps its entire state in `/config` — `config.xml`, `lidarr.db` (main DB, incl. users/auth), `logs.db`, `MediaCover/`, `Backups/`. `/config` is mapped to `/DATA/AppData/lidarr/config`, so no state path is left unmapped. `/music` and `/downloads` are shared user content, not app state. **No data-loss risk on reinstall.** |
| Permission strategy — `user:` field present | **pass (D4)** | `user: $PUID:$PGID` while mounting user dirs `/DATA/Media/Music` + `/DATA/Downloads` → **rule D4** (`$PUID:$PGID`, any path within `/DATA`) → pass; no rationale required |
| Privilege escalation (D5) | **n-a** | No `privileged: true`, no `cap_add` |
| `cpu_shares` present on every service | **pass** | Single service `lidarr` carries `cpu_shares` (value tier is a separate finding below) |
| `name` regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$` | **pass** | `name: lidarr`; `container_name: lidarr` and `x-casaos.main: lidarr` all agree |
| Caddy / Web-UI wiring | **pass** | All three label blocks present; `gateway_tls` imported on `caddy_0`/`caddy_1` and correctly **absent** on `caddy_2`; `{{upstreams 8686}}` matches `expose: 8686`; `pcs` network declared `external: true` |
| Clear description of the application | **pass** | `description` + `tagline` in `en_us`/`fr_fr`/`es_es`/`zh_cn`; `title`, `developer`, `author`, `category`, `tags`, `architectures` all set |
| Volume & environment variable descriptions | **pass** | Per-volume inline comments on all three mounts, plus `tips.before_install` documenting config/music/downloads locations |
| Icon & screenshots meet spec, URLs point to this repo | **pass** | `icon.png`, `screenshot-1.png`, `thumbnail.png` all exist in `Apps/Lidarr/`; all three URLs resolve to `Yundera/AppStore@main` (no contributor fork); thumbnail is a distinct file, not a reused screenshot |

### Failing checklist items

| Item | Verdict | Severity | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Authentication enabled **and documented** | **fail** | **Major** | Lidarr ships no login gate of its own in the compose — no AppShield/OIDC sidecar, no Basic Auth, no `$APP_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` seeding. It relies entirely on Lidarr's own first-launch authentication onboarding. CONTRIBUTING's *Rationale* section requires a `rationale.md` precisely when an app "relies on the app's own first-launch onboarding instead of an enabled default", and `Apps/Lidarr/` contains **no **`rationale.md` (dir holds only the compose + 3 images). The onboarding gate itself is an *acceptable* auth mechanism — the failure is the **missing documented exception**, not an open service. Note: the actual gate could not be exercised (Phase E9 never ran), so this is assessed statically. |
| CPU field `cpu_shares` set **appropriately** | **fail** | **Minor** | `cpu_shares: 10`. Per CPU Share Guidelines, **10 is "System Background (Reserved)"** — reserved for system maintenance tasks. A user-facing media manager with background indexing belongs at **50 (Standard Applications)**, or 30 if deliberately deprioritised. The field is present but the tier is wrong; under load Lidarr would be starved by nearly every other container. (Systemic: `Sonarr`, `Radarr` and `Prowlarr` all ship the same `cpu_shares: 10`, so this is a family-wide fix, not a Lidarr regression.) |
| Proper file permissions based on volume usage | **fail** | **Minor** | The Permission Strategy requires **both** mechanisms: "1 - with the user: `user: xx:xx` **and** 2 - by setting the `PUID` and `PGID` environment variables in the compose file." The compose sets `user: $PUID:$PGID` but its `environment:` block contains only `TZ`. This matters more than usual for a LinuxServer image, whose s6 init uses `PUID`/`PGID` as its documented ownership mechanism. Deviation-table classification is unaffected — **rule D4** still applies and passes. |
| Pre-install command hygiene | **fail** | **Minor** | `pre-install-cmd: mkdir -p /DATA/AppData/lidarr/config "/DATA/Media/Music" /DATA/Downloads` runs on the host and creates directories under the **user dirs** `/DATA/Media` and `/DATA/Downloads`, but never applies `chown -R $PUID:$PGID`. CONTRIBUTING's pre-install requirements call for that "whenever files will live under `/DATA/Documents`, `/DATA/Downloads`, `/DATA/Media`, or `/DATA/Gallery`". If those paths do not already exist as `pcs:pcs`, the container (running as `$PUID:$PGID`) cannot write imports into them. The command is otherwise fine: no `:latest`, non-interactive, no credentials, and `mkdir -p` is naturally idempotent. **This is exactly the class of defect Phase F/G would have confirmed or cleared — and could not.** |

### Deviation table (D1–D5) — applied

| Rule | Applies? | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1 (root, AppData-only) | no | Container is not root |
| D2 (root + user-dir access, no rationale) | no | Container is not root — **this Major finding is *****not***** a D2 fail** |
| D3 (root + rationale covering it) | no | n-a |
| **D4 (**`$PUID:$PGID`**, any path within **`/DATA`**)** | **yes** | **pass** — the correct rule for this compose |
| D5 (`privileged` / `cap_add`) | no | n-a — neither present |

### Static result

## Conclusion

**ERRORED · top severity Major · risk score 13** — retry when the demo pool recovers.

- Lidarr is **not** being blamed: the static review is complete and clean of Critical findings, and its persistence design is sound.
- It is **not** eligible for `compliant` regardless: it carries 1 Major + 3 Minor checklist failures, so even a fully green functional run would land it at **non-compliant · Major (risk 13)**. The Major (missing `rationale.md` for onboarding-based auth) is a one-file fix; the three Minors are one-liners — and `cpu_shares: 10` plus the missing `PUID`/`PGID` env pair should be fixed across the whole Servarr family (`Sonarr`, `Radarr`, `Prowlarr`) at the same time.
- **Blocking issue is infra:** both `demostaging1` and `demostaging2` have been in `❌ Error` (`404`) since 2026-07-31. No app audit at `depth=full` can produce a compliance verdict until at least one instance returns to `✅ Ready` with more than 1h remaining.
